content: The 2014 edition of the International Drug Price Indicator Guide, which is updated annually, was accessed on June 6, 2016. Rustomjee et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial comparing azithromycin with doxycycline/ciprofloxacin for the syndromic management of sexually transmitted infections in resource-limited settings, published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2002 (Volume 49, Issue 5, Pages 875-878). Chauhan et al. performed an audit on the use of benzathine penicillin, post-treatment syphilis serology, and partner notification in patients with early infectious syphilis, published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2006 (Volume 17, Issue 3, Pages 200-202). Crow et al. evaluated the acceptability and compliance of daily procaine penicillin injections for outpatient treatment of syphilis, published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 1997 (Volume 24, Issue 3, Pages 127-130). Kingston and Higgins audited the management of early syphilis at North Manchester General Hospital, published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2004 (Volume 15, Issue 5, Pages 352-354). Tayal et al. conducted an audit of early syphilis cases in Teesside from 2005 to 2007, published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2009 (Volume 20, Issue 9, Pages 647-649). Nagarkar and Mhaskar performed a systematic review on the prevalence and healthcare utilization for reproductive tract infections and sexually transmitted infections in India, published in the Indian Journal of Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2015 (Volume 36, Issue 1, Pages 18-25). Ryan et al. provided an overview of systematic reviews on interventions to improve safe and effective medicine use by consumers, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 4, Article CD007768). Dixon-Woods et al. conducted a qualitative study on women’s views regarding the selection and use of sexual health services, published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2001 (Volume 77, Issue 5, Pages 335-339). The World Health Organization (WHO) released a report on global sexually transmitted infection surveillance in 2015, with an earlier report from 2013 accessed on June 6, 2016. Unemo and Nicholas highlighted the emergence of multidrug-resistant, extensively drug-resistant, and untreatable gonorrhea, published in Future Microbiology in 2012 (Volume 7, Pages 1401-1422). Unemo et al. documented two cases of verified clinical failures using cefixime for gonorrhea treatment in Norway in 2010, published in Euro Surveillance in 2010 (Volume 15, Issue 47, Article 19721). Ison et al. reported treatment failures with cefixime and azithromycin for gonorrhea in England in 2010, published in Euro Surveillance in 2011 (Volume 16, Issue 14, Article 19833). Unemo et al. described high-level cefiximeand ceftriaxone-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae in France, linked to a novel penA mosaic allele, published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2012 (Volume 56, Issue 3, Pages 1273-1280). Unemo et al. reported the first Neisseria gonorrhoeae strain resistant to cefixime causing treatment failure in Austria, published in Euro Surveillance in 2011 (Volume 16, Issue 43, Article 19998). Lewis et al. characterized the first two cases of extended-spectrum cephalosporin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae in South Africa, associated with cefixime treatment failure, published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2013 (Volume 68, Issue 6, Pages 1267-1270). Allen et al. documented Neisseria gonorrhoeae treatment failure and susceptibility to cefixime in Toronto, Canada, published in JAMA in 2013 (Volume 309, Issue 2, Pages 163-170). Yokoi et al. raised concerns about cefixime treatment for gonorrhea in Japan, published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2007 (Volume 13, Issue 8, Pages 1275-1277). Unemo et al. reported ceftriaxone treatment failure for pharyngeal gonorrhea in Sweden in 2010, published in Euro Surveillance in 2011 (Volume 16, Issue 6, Article 19792). Chen et al. documented the failure of 500 mg ceftriaxone to eradicate pharyngeal gonorrhea in Australia, published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2013 (Volume 68, Issue 6, Pages 1445-1447). Unemo et al. verified treatment failure of pharyngeal gonorrhea with ceftriaxone in Slovenia in 2011, published in Euro Surveillance in 2012 (Volume 17, Issue 25, Article 20200). Ohnishi et al. provided detailed characterization of the first strain with high-level resistance to ceftriaxone, published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2011 (Volume 55, Issue 7, Pages 3538-3545). High ceftriaxone minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values in Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains have been reported in Japan (H041 strain), France, Spain (F89 strain), and Australia (A8806 strain). Unemo et al. described the emergence of high-level azithromycin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates in Sweden, published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2014 (Volume 58, Issue 1, Pages 624-625). Morita-Ishihara et al. reported treatment failure with 2 g azithromycin in Japan due to the multidrug-resistant ST1407 strain, published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2014 (Volume 69, Issue 8, Pages 2086-2090). Ison et al. documented gonorrhea treatment failures with cefixime and azithromycin in England in 2010, published in Euro Surveillance. Allen et al. reported azithromycin resistance co-evolving with reduced susceptibility to cephalosporins in Ontario, Canada, published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2014 (Volume 58, Issue 5, Pages 2528-2534). Tanaka et al. highlighted a high prevalence of azithromycin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates in Fukuoka, Japan, published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2015 (Volume 42, Issue 6, Pages 337-341). Młynarczyk-Bonikowska et al. reported azithromycin resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains isolated in Poland in 2012-2013, published in Medical Dosw Microbiol in 2014. Stevens et al. documented Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates with high-level azithromycin resistance in Australia, published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2015 (Volume 70, Issue 4, Pages 1267-1268). Starnino et al. analyzed antimicrobial susceptibility trends in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from Latin America and the Caribbean, published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2012 (Volume 39, Issue 10, Pages 813-821). Gose et al. reported high-level azithromycin resistance in California, published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2015 (Volume 42, Pages 279-280). Shigemura et al. described azithromycin resistance mechanisms in Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains in Hyogo, Japan, published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2015 (Volume 59, Issue 5, Pages 2695-2699). Katz et al. reported the first Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolate with high-level azithromycin resistance in the United States, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2012 (Volume 54, Issue 6, Pages 841-843). Yuan et al. documented azithromycin resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from two cities in China, published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2011 (Volume 38, Issue 8, Pages 764-768). Lynagh et al. characterized the first high-level azithromycin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae cases in Ireland, published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2015 (Volume 70, Issue 8, Pages 2411-2413). Bercot et al. reported a high-level azithromycin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae clinical isolate in France in 2014, published in Euro Surveillance (Volume 19, Issue 44, Article 20951). Galarza et al. described the emergence of high-level azithromycin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae in Argentina, published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2009 (Volume 36, Pages 787-788). Fransen et al. evaluated single-dose kanamycin therapy for gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum, published in The Lancet in 1984 (Volume 2, Issue 8414, Pages 1234-1237). Gururaj et al. reviewed changing trends in the epidemiology and management of gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the Singapore Medical Journal in 1992 (Volume 33, Issue 3, Pages 279-281). Haase et al. assessed single-dose ceftriaxone therapy for gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum, published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 1986 (Volume 13, Issue 1, Pages 53-55). Hira et al. studied ophthalmia neonatorum in Zambia, published in the European Journal of Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 1986 (Volume 3, Issue 2, Pages 103-106). Hoosen et al. evaluated single low-dose ceftriaxone for gonococcal ophthalmia treatment, published in the South African Medical Journal in 2002 (Volume 92, Issue 3, Pages 238-240). Jarvis reviewed a decade of experience with ophthalmia neonatorum at Mount Sinai Hospital, published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology in 1987 (Volume 71, Issue 4, Pages 295-300). Laga et al. compared single-dose ceftriaxone therapy for gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1986 (Volume 315, Issue 22, Pages 1382-1385). Latif et al. managed gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum with single-dose kanamycin and saline irrigation, published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 1988 (Volume 15, Issue 2, Pages 108-109). Lepage et al. demonstrated the efficacy of single-dose intramuscular cefotaxime for gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology in 1988 (Volume 72, Issue 7, Pages 518-520). Lepage et al. further evaluated cefotaxime for gonococcal conjunctivitis, published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 1990 (Volume 26, Supplement A, Pages 23-27). Li et al. conducted clinical research on neonatal gonococcal conjunctivitis treated with ceftriaxone, published in the International Journal of Ophthalmology in 2009 (Volume 9, Issue 5, Pages 1000-1001). Lockie et al. identified penicillinase-producing Neisseria gonorrhoeae as a cause of neonatal and adult ophthalmia, published in the Australian and New Zealand Journal of Ophthalmology. Ng et al. reviewed ophthalmia neonatorum cases at Middle Road Hospital, published in the Annals of the Academy of Medicine Singapore in 1987 (Volume 6, Issue 4, Pages 645-647). Nsanze et al. studied ophthalmia neonatorum in the United Arab Emirates, published in the Annals of Tropical Paediatrics (Volume 16, Issue 1, Pages 27-32). Rajan et al. evaluated treatment for gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the Singapore Medical Journal in 1978 (Volume 19, Issue 2, Pages 86-88). Deogan et al. conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of a community-based intervention to reduce chlamydia prevalence in Sweden, published in the Scandinavian Journal of Public Health in 2010 (Volume 38, Issue 2, Pages 141-150). Zuppa et al. reviewed prophylaxis for ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the Journal of Maternal-Fetal & Neonatal Medicine in 2011 (Volume 24, Issue 6, Pages 769-773). Kapoor et al. reviewed interventions for preventing ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 1999 (Issue 4, Article CD001862). Darling and McDonald conducted a meta-analysis on the efficacy of ocular prophylactic agents for preventing gonococcal and chlamydial ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health in 2010 (Volume 55, Issue 4, Pages 319-327). Mabry-Hernandez and Koenig reaffirmed recommendations for preventive services, published by the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality in 2010. Ali et al. compared the efficacy of betadine, erythromycin, and no prophylaxis for ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the Journal of Tropical Pediatrics in 2007 (Volume 53, Issue 6, Pages 388-392). Brussieux et al. compared silver nitrate and oxytetracycline eye drops for neonatal conjunctivitis prevention, published in Annales de Pédiatrie in 1991 (Volume 38, Issue 9, Pages 637-641). Chen compared silver nitrate, tetracycline, erythromycin, and no prophylaxis for ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 1992 (Volume 11, Issue 12, Pages 1026-1030). David et al. evaluated the efficacy of povidone-iodine and tetracycline for ophthalmia neonatorum prevention, published in Ophthalmology in 2011 (Volume 118, Issue 7, Pages 1454-1458). Fischer and Reta studied neonatal conjunctivitis prevention in Zaire, published in the Annals of Tropical Paediatrics in 1988 (Volume 8, Issue 2, Pages 85-86). Hammerschlag et al. assessed neonatal ocular prophylaxis for chlamydial and gonococcal conjunctivitis prevention, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1989 (Volume 320, Issue 12, Pages 769-772). Hammerschlag et al. evaluated erythromycin ointment for neonatal chlamydial infection prophylaxis, published in JAMA in 1980 (Volume 244, Issue 20, Pages 2291-2293). Isenberg et al. compared silver nitrate and erythromycin for ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis, published in Clinical Pediatrics in 1992 (Volume 31, Issue 5, Pages 295-298). Knapp et al. documented the frequency and distribution of tetracycline-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains in the United States, published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 1987 (Volume 155, Issue 4, Pages 819-822). Ison et al. reported tetracycline-resistant gonococci in the UK, published in The Lancet in 1988 (Volume 1, Issue 8586, Pages 651-652). Schwarcz et al. conducted national surveillance of antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, published in JAMA in 1990 (Volume 264, Issue 11, Pages 1413-1417). Hedberg et al. reported an outbreak of erythromycin-resistant staphylococcal conjunctivitis in a newborn nursery, published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 1990 (Volume 9, Issue 4, Pages 268-273). Deogan et al. analyzed the cost-effectiveness of a community-based intervention to reduce chlamydia prevalence in Sweden, published in the Scandinavian Journal of Public Health in 2010 (Volume 38, Issue 2, Pages 141-150). Keenan et al. conducted a cost analysis of povidone-iodine for ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis, published in Archives of Ophthalmology in 2010 (Volume 128, Issue 1, Pages 136-137). Kakar et al. identified Chlamydia trachomatis as a cause of neonatal conjunctivitis in a tertiary care center, published in the Indian Journal of Medical Microbiology in 2010 (Volume 28, Issue 1, Pages 45-47). Darling and McDonald conducted a meta-analysis on the efficacy of ocular prophylactic agents for preventing gonococcal and chlamydial ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health in 2010 (Volume 55, Issue 4, Pages 319-327).
